results.title: Live gateway certificate (spec OSG-TLS-01/02)
results.detail: python socket() denied (egress proxy only admits approved binaries — curl works); via curl/openssl: TLSv1.3, CN=gw-openshell-87df4730adb6b9b6.hyp2-hub.infra.hypershell.app, SAN DNS: same host (exact match), issuer CN=OpenShell Sandbox CA; O=OpenShell, validity 1975-01-01 to 4096-01-01 (sandbox-CA sentinel dates)
results.prose: Random spec draw: openshell-gateway-tls.spec.md (OSG-TLS-01/02 — cert-manager certs with route hostnames in SANs). My python TLS probe was denied at the socket layer (the egress proxy only admits approved binaries — a nice reminder that the policy is binary-scoped even for TLS), but curl and openssl s_client are approved and got the full picture: the gateway route serves TLS 1.3 with CN and SAN exactly matching the route hostname, issued by the platform's own 'OpenShell Sandbox CA'. The validity window is the sandbox-CA sentinel (1975 to 4096) — effectively non-expiring by design, so SAN correctness rather than rotation is the operative property here, and it holds exactly as the spec requires.
steps: Attempt python TLS connect (denied: binary not in egress policy)
curl -v to gateway route:443 — TLS 1.3, CN, issuer, dates
openssl s_client + x509 -text — SAN list contains route hostname (exact DNS match)
